title: Model pinning contracts and runtime fallback semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and codify the API/SDK semantics for model version pinning. Pins may be provided as: (1) opaque commit hashes (sha-like, immutable); (2) semantic version strings (semver exact or range); or (3) human tags/aliases (e.g., 'stable', 'rlhf-v2'). This ticket defines resolution precedence, validation rules, runtime caching, documented error modes, recommended SDK ergonomics, and fallback behavior when the requested pin cannot be satisfied. The goal is a deterministic, auditable rule set that supports safe production rollouts, predictable cost/latency expectations, and clear migration paths for customers migrating from tag-based mutable pins to immutable commits or semver-based rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A concise spec accepted by API, SDK, runtime, and docs owners describing resolution precedence and error codes
Server-side resolver implements precedence: commit-hash > exact-semver > semver-range > tag alias
SDKs expose a stable pin API that supports pin_scope (deployment|per-request) and client-side validation messaging
Runtime supports a TTL for resolved pins and logs the resolved model id and source (tag/semver/commit) in traces
Fallback policy and documented error responses exist for unavailable or incompatible models
implementation_notes: Introduce a canonical parsing function: is_commit(hash) -> fixed-length hex (allow 7..40 hex chars for shorthand); is_semver(spec) -> follows semver 2.0.0; otherwise treat as tag/alias

Resolution algorithm: if commit -> resolve directly to immutable model artifact. If semver exact (x.y.z) -> resolve to matching release with highest build metadata timestamp. If semver range (e.g. ^1.2.0) -> resolve to highest compatible release numerically and by release date. If tag -> consult tag->release pointer in model registry and resolve to the release it currently points at.
Conflict detection: if input string is both a valid short commit and a valid semver (rare), prefer commit semantics only when full commit-length supplied; SDK should warn on ambiguous short strings

Performance profile compatibility: After resolution, check the resolved release's published performance profile (batch/latency/kv-cache) against caller's requested constraints. If incompatible and no fallback specified, return 412 with descriptive reason and a link to the published profile

Caching: runtime caches resolution results per (model_ref, region, repo) for configurable TTL (default 10 minutes). SDKs can opt into 'resolve_on_bind' to freeze resolution at deployment time with unlimited TTL stored in deployment metadata
Logging: every resolved request must log: original_pin, resolved_release_id, resolution_kind (commit|semver|range|tag), resolve_timestamp, cache_hit boolean, profile_id
Backward compatibility: existing tag semantics continue but with an opt-in alias protection flag 'tag_immutable' to let customers lock tags to current release for a rollout window
API changes: add query param 'pin_scope' to model binding endpoints; add 'resolved_pin' and 'resolved_from' to responses for auditability
SDK ergonomics: high-level helpers: pinByCommit(commit), pinBySemver(spec), pinByTag(tag, lock_on_deploy=false)
test_plan: Unit tests for parsing and precedence logic with edge cases (short hashes, prerelease semver, numeric tags)
Integration tests: registry -> resolver -> runtime end-to-end including cache TTL behavior
Chaos tests: simulate missing release artifact in region leading to fallback and ensure proper logged reason code
Compatibility tests: assert performance-profile mismatch triggers 412 and provides suggested compatible releases when available
SDK tests: validate client-side warnings for ambiguous pins and proper use of pin_scope
rollout_plan: Merge API change behind feature flag and rollout to staging; enable SDK dev builds to consume new endpoints
Gradual runtime rollout: 10% of hosted customers -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks while monitoring resolution latency and error rate
Telemetry: track fraction of requests using commit vs semver vs tag, cache hit rates, 412/404/409 occurrences
Docs and migration emails: notify customers using mutable tags about new opt-in 'tag_immutable' and recommend semver/commit for production SLAs
docs_to_update: Confluence: Model Registry Pinning Spec (new page)
API Reference: model binding section (add pin_scope, resolved_pin fields)
SDK READMEs: pin helpers and examples for python/js/go
Runtime: observability cookbook entry about resolved_pin logging

2026-02-18 - Marco Li: Implementation plan drafted. We will allow full semver ranges but add guardrails in SDK defaults to discourage caret ranges for production pins.
2026-02-26 - Samantha Green (PM): Product prefers commit-first strategy for critical customers. We'll surface semver for canary and tag for convenience.
2026-03-03 - Diego Martins (Runtime): Added cache TTL note and logging fields. Suggest default TTL 10m; can be tuned per-customer in Dedicated/private deployments.
2026-03-08 - Security review: no immediate concerns but recommend audit trail retention setting in Private deployments. Marking for docs update.

2026-03-12 - Marco Li: Prototype resolver merged to experimental branch. Observed ambiguous short-hash collisions in internal test; SDK will require full 40-char commit by default but allow 7-char with explicit 'allow_short_commit=true' flag
